status: post-hoc diagnostic registered before new resource observations
trigger: All 112 previously completed filecheck samples reported peak_rss_kib=35072, so launcher history may dominate the process high-water mark.
new_binary: A small C supervisor only. It records its current VmHWM/VmRSS and getrusage, forks a child, records the child's pre-exec floor, execs the unchanged filecheck argv, and obtains wait4 rusage.
ordering: rotate arms by group plus algorithm index; reverse on odd groups

parent_memory_control.launch_order: direct first on even groups, supervisor first on odd groups
parent_memory_control.scope: Finite intervention on launcher residency; not a proof of all kernel accounting paths. Padding stays live throughout padded controls. No ordinary controls occur after padding.

resource_metrics: Python launcher VmHWM, VmRSS and RUSAGE_SELF ru_maxrss
unit: KiB on the recorded Linux host
identity_policy: Hash original qualification report, driver, each library and input before observations and again after; recheck driver/library/input at every invocation. Hash diagnostic source, compiler and supervisor. Pathname execution on a trusted host, not a sealed-image certificate.
failure_policy: No retries or exclusions. Retain every started invocation's stdout, stderr, metadata and failure status.
timing_policy: Original program timing fields remain in raw stdout for provenance only. No supplementary latency or throughput summaries, performance winner selection, or replacement of any of the 112 original samples.
interpretation: Report medians and ranges of resource observations, show controlled launch-floor effects, and state whether the evidence supports a launch-history contribution. RSS includes runtime, loader and shared pages; it is not live HIA owner bytes or a resource safety theorem.
reference_observation: Linux man-pages documents ru_maxrss in KiB and preservation of resource usage metrics across execve; the fork/exec control is still measured rather than presumed correct.
